question: Electrons are accelerated through a potential difference such that their de Broglie wavelength becomes comparable to the spacing between atoms in a crystal. Why is a crystal suitable for observing diffraction of such electrons?

options.A: A crystal is suitable because it absorbs electrons completely and prevents any scattering.
options.B: A crystal has regularly spaced atomic planes whose separation is comparable to the de Broglie wavelength of suitably accelerated electrons. It therefore produces coherent scattering and acts as a diffraction grating for electron waves.
options.C: A crystal is suitable because electrons become photons after striking its atoms.
options.D: A crystal is suitable only because its atoms are randomly arranged and scatter electrons in all directions equally.
